description: Sierra Leone NIN format derived from real eID card samples (the field labelled 'NIN'): 8 uppercase alphanumeric characters, no country prefix and no embedded year. The long 'SL...' number on the card is the separate Personal ID Number, not the NIN. Exact charset constraints and any checksum are still unconfirmed by NCRA — edit this file to change behaviour without code changes (Architecture Spec section 4.1 and 12.1). Edits are validated at load: 'charset' must be anchored with ^ and $, and 'checksum.algorithm' must be a known algorithm, or the SDK throws InvalidNinFormatSchemaError naming the field. DO NOT set checksum.enabled to true yet: the only wired algorithm is Luhn, which runs over the NIN's decimal digits and therefore rejects all-letter NINs — a shape observed on a real card. It is a placeholder awaiting an NCRA-confirmed algorithm suited to an alphanumeric identifier.
